subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Loss Aversion in Negotiations
description: One-minute skill: Loss Aversion in Negotiations.

hook.text: A seller won't accept $450,000 for a house they paid $500,000 for. The market dropped. They still can't let go.

buildup.text: Genesove and Mayer found that real estate owners set asking prices based on what they paid, not market value.

discovery.text: Loss aversion in negotiation: concessions feel like losses. Each dollar you give up stings more than each dollar gained.

twist.text: Framing concessions as gains changes behavior. 'You're getting a premium location' works better than 'the price.

climax.text: Effective negotiators frame offers to minimize the other side's perceived losses. Language reshapes the deal.

quiz.question: How does loss aversion affect negotiation?
options: Concessions feel like painful losses, making deals harder
